content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with [product_name] V8.3 software to handle around 10 different analog values. I need to send the maximum value to an analog output. Could someone explain how I can connect these values?
You should use an analog MUX function.
Hello, thanks for your response. I already tried using the analog MUX, but it seems like I can only include four values.
You can cascade several analog MUX units to handle more values.
Where can I locate this module?
Hello, thanks for your helpful reply. How can I format values to show one or two decimal places using the MUX module? I set it to one decimal, but still can't input decimal numbers.

The [product_name] system processes values as integers. Decimal places are only represented visually on the display. For example, to display 50.6, you should enter 506 in the block and set the display to show one decimal place. For 50.61, input 5061 and set it for two decimal places.

analysis.insight_summary: Users utilizing [product_name] notice that its analog MUX feature only allows four inputs, prompting solutions like cascading modules to handle more values. There is also confusion about decimal handling, since real numbers are stored as integers and decimal formatting is managed through display settings and not internally.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to manage more than four analog values easily in a single operation and want simple options to work with values showing one or two decimal places through the software interface.
